fact: DHIS2 states that almost 99 percent of public health facilities already used DHIS2 for health service reporting before the eLMIS project launched in 2024; the share is of all public facilities (the document counts 74 sites), not of primary clinics alone, with no numerator given and no statement of where the reports are keyed.

DHIS2 states that the national DHIS2 platform is the Ministry of Health's, that local Ministry staff are being trained to maintain DHIS2 configurations and dashboards, and that HISP Rwanda leads customisation and capacity building with maintenance being handed over to the Ministry, as of November 2025.

WHO Comoros reports DHIS2 extended to 91 public-level health structures in 2025, which it gives as 100% of public-level structures; the figure is of all public structures the system reaches, not of primary clinics alone, and the report does not say whether each structure keys its own reports.

WHO Comoros states DHIS2 reached all 91 public-level health structures (100%) in 2025 and calls this a national extension; the report names no tier, so every tier is read from 'all public structures' only.

During 2025, with WHO support, DHIS2 was extended to the 91 public structures, validation rules were put into DHIS2, a data quality self-assessment (DQS) was run, a standard data-management procedures manual was written and the WHO SCORE survey and an assessment of the health information system's functionality were carried out.

WHO Comoros lists among the health information system's weaknesses before 2023 that DHIS2 had not been put in place at national scale, and says that before DHIS2 the data sat in scattered, non-centralised Excel files; it does not say reporting was on paper.

In 2024, with WHO support, 170 health workers were trained in managing and analysing data in DHIS2 with the WHO Data Quality Tool built in, the first quarterly health information bulletins were published and the 2021 and 2022 health statistical yearbooks were produced; WHO Comoros says health structures and all districts can now see health information in real time.

The World Bank's results framework for project P175840 counts 69 public health facilities reporting data in DHIS2 at 31 August 2024, from a baseline of 0 in May 2021 and against a target of 80 by December 2025; it gives no denominator and does not split primary clinics from hospitals.

The World Bank reports the successful deployment of DHIS2 as the new health information system as a key achievement of the project, with more than 60 facilities reporting data through it so that programmes can monitor key indicators; the indicator stood at 69 on both 23 May 2024 and 31 August 2024.

DHIS2 was deployed under component 2 (health system strengthening, cost USD 24.7 million) of the World Bank IDA-financed project P175840, whose implementing agency is the Ministry of Health; the report names no domestic funding for the system.

The Ministry of Health's strategy of July 2021 says the national health information system (SNIS) is semi-electronic, computerised at the level of the regions on GESIS, with data passing from districts to regions by hand or by e-mail; the keying level it names is the region, above the district.

The strategy states that the Ministry of Health is deploying DHIS2 under the supervision of its Direction de l'Information et des Statistiques Sanitaires (DISS), which is to be responsible for operating the SNIS databases.

The Stratégie Nationale de Santé Numérique 2022-2026 names DHIS2 in project P221, strengthening and extension of the SNIS with DHIS2, scheduled January 2022 to December 2025 and costed at USD 0.60 million, and recommends DHIS2 as the single SNIS for the whole ministry including the vertical programmes.

The strategy says the DHIS2 deployment is financed by the Global Fund, and its financing table puts the whole USD 0.60 million of the SNIS extension project against technical and financial partners, with nothing against the Ministry of Health.

As at July 2021 the Ministry of Health was in the course of deploying DHIS2 with Global Fund technical and financial support, the one part of the previous digital health strategy's action plan carried out, the rest having gone unimplemented for lack of funds.

The Ministry of Health's strategy of July 2021 states that the electronic patient record (Dossier Electronique du Patient) does not exist in the country, listing it with telemedicine, m-health applications and online training as components that are absent.
